rules.description: The prior bar is an outside bar and the always-in direction is not long, the case in which Brooks allows only the with-trend breakout.

complexity.reason: needs the always-in state, a persistent cross-bar read

catalog_match.note: No always-in or outside-bar rule in the catalog.

rules.merge_notes: Positive composite, placed negated so only with-trend breakouts of an outside bar survive. Uses the agreed always-in definition (AlwaysInDirection, two consecutive strong trend bars), so it is not blocked on a design decision; it is B only because that primitive has to exist first.

rules.description: The current bar is an outside bar and the bar before it was not a decent bull reversal bar (a bull body closing near its high).

complexity.reason: the outside-bar test plus a single-bar body and close-position test

catalog_match.note: The reversal-bar half resembles CloseRangePosition but is measured on the prior bar and combined with a body sign.

rules.merge_notes: Positive composite, placed negated to reproduce Brooks's rule that a reversal entry on an outside bar needs a decent signal bar before it. The reversal-bar definition is inlined from bar_anatomy_trend_doji's family and should be reconciled with whatever that bucket names it.

rules.description: Each of the session's first N bars extended the move with no pause, every one making a higher high than the bar before it (mirrored down).
rules.pseudocode: barsSinceSessionStart >= noPauseBars && for i in 0..noPauseBars-1: high[i] > high[i+1]

complexity.reason: needs a session-bar counter reset on each new date, plus a short window loop

catalog_match.note: No session-structure rule in the catalog; CalendarBoundaryExit reads Date but for a different purpose.

rules.merge_notes: Brooks says the odds of a reversal rise when the market has not paused by the third or fourth bar; the tradeable form is this run test placed negated (or used as a countertrend permission). Only the odds statement is discretionary, the bar test is not. Low source confidence, so treat the defaults as a starting point.

rules.description: The bar that ends a pullback within an existing bull leg - the first bar to make a higher high after at least one down close - is itself a strong bull reversal bar (mirror in a bear leg).
rules.pseudocode: close[1] < open[1] && high[0] > high[1] && bullReversalBarShape[0] && close[0] > close[pullbackLookback]

complexity.reason: the shape test plus a pullback-end test plus a momentum context term

catalog_match.note: The close[0] > close[pullbackLookback] term is exactly Momentum(pullbackLookback); the rest is new.

rules.merge_notes: The source records this as the High-1 proxy WITHOUT the leg counter - the mechanizable reading MERGE.md asks for, so it stays here rather than going to leg_counting. The Momentum term is a carried catalog rule and could be split off at authoring time; kept in the pseudocode because without it the rule fires on every pullback in a downtrend too.

rules.description: Within the last N bars there is evidence of directional pressure at this level: either at least K bars with a prominent tail on the relevant side, OR at least K bars with a strong same-direction body.
rules.pseudocode: countIf(k in 0..pressureLookback-1: (high[k] - max(open[k], close[k])) >= minTailFraction * (high[k] - low[k])) >= minPressureBars || countIf(k in 0..pressureLookback-1: close[k] < open[k] && (open[k] - close[k]) >= minBodyFraction * (high[k] - low[k])) >= minPressureBars

complexity.reason: two window counts of two different per-bar classifications, combined with an OR

catalog_match.note: Same CountIF machinery; different counted conditions, and an OR between two counts rather than a comparison between them.

rules.merge_notes: This is UpperTailCountInWindow OR StrongBodyBarCountInWindow at their own thresholds. Normally a composite would be dropped in favour of its parts, but the pane system ANDs entries, so the OR cannot be composed - carried whole for that reason, with both parts also carried separately.

rules.description: After N consecutive bull trend bars, the first bar that closes DOWN is bought at the next open (short: after N bear trend bars, the first up-closing bar is sold) - the countertrend bar is expected to fail immediately.
rules.pseudocode: for k in 1..runBars: close[k] > open[k] && (close[k] - open[k]) >= bodyFraction * (high[k] - low[k]); && close[0] < open[0]

complexity.reason: a run of the per-bar classification at lag 1 plus an opposite-direction test on bar 0

rules.merge_notes: R28-20 ('buy a bear close after at least a couple of strong bull trend bars at the start of a strong bull swing') and T18-11 ('buying the close of the first bear bar in a bull spike') are the same bars; R28-20's 'start of a strong swing' qualifier is a research-grade context read and is dropped, which is what keeps the merged rule out of grade C. Not composable: the long side needs a BEAR bar at lag 0 and BULL bars at lags 1..N, and a placement's flip toggle reverses both halves at once. Distinct from SpikePullbackLimitFade, which enters on a price poke below the prior low with no requirement that the bar close down.

rules.description: Two large bull trend bars within M bars of each other, separated by at least one bar that is not a bull trend bar (short: mirrored) - Brooks's consecutive climaxes.
rules.pseudocode: largeBullTrendBar[0] && exists k in 2..maxGapBars: (largeBullTrendBar[k] && exists j in 1..k-1: !bullTrendBar[j])

complexity.reason: a short backward scan for a second qualifying bar with a pause between, on top of an ATR window

rules.merge_notes: Not composable: 'two large trend bars with a pause between them' is a pattern over a variable offset, not an AND of per-bar tests. Kept here rather than sent to climax_reversal because the pattern is stated entirely in bar anatomy; T21-37, which needs a swing low and a trend-age counter, went to that bucket instead.

rules.description: Each of the last N bars is a STRONG bull trend bar (short: strong bear): body at least a fraction of its range AND both tails no more than a small fraction of its range. Brooks's always-in flip test.
rules.pseudocode: for k in 0..consecutiveBars-1: close[k] > open[k] && (close[k] - open[k]) >= bodyFraction * (high[k] - low[k]) && (high[k] - close[k]) <= tailFraction * (high[k] - low[k]) && (open[k] - low[k]) <= tailFraction * (high[k] - low[k])

complexity.reason: a fixed-length loop over a three-part per-bar classification; the tail terms cannot be ANDed in from other panes because they must hold on each bar of the run

catalog_match.note: ConsecutiveUpBars tests only close vs the bar's own open; this adds the body-size and both-tail tests to every bar of the run.

rules.merge_notes: V15-01 and V16-01 are the reversals volume's two identical definitions of the strong trend bar (body >= 0.6 of range, each tail <= 0.2 of range); they are carried here as citations rather than as their own rule, because a standalone strong-trend-bar test is just TrendBarBody AND CloseRangePosition AND OpenNearBarLow, which the entry pane already ANDs. What is NOT composable is requiring all three on each bar of a RUN, which is this rule. Brooks: 'there usually has to have been at least two consecutive strong bull trend bars before most traders will believe that the always-in direction is long'; default consecutiveBars 2 as stated. This is the recommended definition for the always-in design decision.

rules.description: The previous bar was a large bear trend bar (range above K times the ATR) and this bar is a doji: a possible sell climax and reversal - enter long at the next open. Short is the mirror.
rules.pseudocode: close[1] < open[1] && (open[1] - close[1]) >= bodyFraction * (high[1] - low[1]) && (high[1] - low[1]) >= bigBarMultiple * atr(atrLookback) && abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= dojiFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: an ATR window plus fixed-offset bar tests across two bars

rules.merge_notes: Kept whole rather than split into TrendBarBody + BarRangeAboveAtrMultiple + DojiBar: the first two terms are evaluated at lag 1 with the direction OPPOSITE to the trade, the third at lag 0, and the panes cannot mix lags. A named two-bar Brooks reversal, mechanized under the standing close-then-next-open convention.

rules.description: The session's first bar is a small doji that sits entirely inside the high-low range of the previous session's last N bars: a stronger range-day bias than a doji open alone. Identical both sides.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.SessionDate(0) != ctx.SessionDate(1) && abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= dojiFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (high[0] - low[0]) <= dojiRangeFraction * atr(atrLookback) && low[0] >= lowest(low, closingRangeBars)[1] && high[0] <= highest(high, closingRangeBars)[1]

complexity.reason: a session boundary, a doji test, an ATR window and a containment test against the prior session's last bars

rules.merge_notes: Kept apart from FirstBarOfSessionDoji: the containment test in yesterday's closing range is what Brooks adds, and the two fire on different days. Note it does NOT latch, unlike FirstBarOfSessionDoji - the mining agent recorded it as a one-bar filter and the book's wording supports either reading; the authoring pass should pick one and note it. closingRangeBars = 5 is a guess, Brooks gives no count.

rules.description: The first bar of the session was a doji - latched for the rest of the session as a trading-range-day bias, favouring fades over breakout continuation. Identical both sides.
rules.pseudocode: if ctx.SessionDate(0) != ctx.SessionDate(1) then rangeDayBias = abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= dojiFraction * (high[0] - low[0]); // rangeDayBias holds for the rest of the session

complexity.reason: a session-boundary test plus a latch that persists the verdict across the session's remaining bars

rules.merge_notes: Both sources state the same test. Kept as a rule rather than dropped as DojiBar AND a session filter, because the book's point is the LATCH: the doji fires once, at the open, and biases the whole day. Without the latch it would fire on one bar a day and gate nothing. Book values 0.1 (R21-15) and 0.25 (VP3-04); default 0.25.

rules.description: The first bar of the session closed as a bull trend bar: take a scalp long at the next open. Short is the mirror.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.SessionDate(0) != ctx.SessionDate(1) && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: a session-boundary test plus a single-bar classification

rules.merge_notes: Kept rather than dropped as a composition because the session-boundary primitive is not carried in this bucket and because it is the anchor of the FirstBarSessionTrendBarFailureReversal pair, which Brooks states together. Brooks frames the exit as a scalp; only the entry is mined.

rules.description: The session's first bar was a bull trend bar and the second bar is a bear trend bar closing below the first bar's open: the long setup failed, enter short at the next open. Long is the mirror.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.SessionDate(1) != ctx.SessionDate(2) && close[1] > open[1] && (close[1] - open[1]) >= bodyFraction * (high[1] - low[1]) && close[0] < open[0] && (open[0] - close[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && close[0] < open[1]

complexity.reason: a two-bar pattern anchored on the session boundary, otherwise fixed-offset comparisons

rules.merge_notes: Not composable in any direction: the trade is SHORT while the first bar is BULL. Brooks gives no numeric failure threshold; 'the second bar closes below the first bar's open' is the mining agent's reading and is the tunable part of the rule.

rules.description: After N consecutive bull trend bars, the current bar trades below the previous bar's low (the first weak pullback bar): buy, betting the pullback fails and the spike resumes. Short is the mirror.
rules.pseudocode: for k in 1..spikeBars: close[k] > open[k] && (close[k] - open[k]) >= bodyFraction * (high[k] - low[k]); && low[0] <= low[1]

complexity.reason: the consecutive-trend-bar run evaluated at lag 1, plus a touch-of-level test standing in for the limit fill

catalog_match.note: The pullback half is LaggedHigherHigh(0) negated and flipped; the run half is ConsecutiveTrendBars at lag 1. Kept whole because the run must END one bar before the pullback bar, an offset no pane can supply.

rules.merge_notes: Three statements of the same setup - V03-10 (5 bars, limit at the prior bar's extreme), VP3-10 (2 bars, limit at or below the doji's low), V19-05 (2 bars, the first bar that pokes past the prior bar's extreme). V19-05 phrases it as a with-trend stop entry and the other two as a limit entry, but all three fire on the same bar; the limit fill is approximated by the bar trading through the level, as the mining brief allows. Default spikeBars 2 (two of the three sources).

rules.description: Somewhere in the last N bars there was a run of at least R consecutive bull trend bars (short: bear) - earlier strength, not necessarily still in progress. Negate for Brooks's 'the rally never produced two consecutive strong bull trend bars'.
rules.pseudocode: exists i in 0..lookback-runBars: for all j in 0..runBars-1: close[i+j] > open[i+j] && (close[i+j] - open[i+j]) >= bodyFraction * (high[i+j] - low[i+j])

complexity.reason: a nested window scan for a run anywhere in the lookback, rather than a run ending at the current bar

rules.merge_notes: T07-38 ('a strong bull trend bar occurred within the last K bars, so a high 2 pullback may be bought') is this rule at runBars = 1; V01-12 ('the rally did not contain two consecutive strong bull trend bars') is it at runBars = 2, negated. One rule with a parameter and the negate toggle. Kept apart from ConsecutiveTrendBars, which requires the run to end at the current bar: 'strength ten bars ago' and 'strength right now' fire on different bars. T07-38 also required range >= average range on the run's bars; that term is dropped here (AND in BarRangeAboveAtrMultiple is not equivalent inside a scan, so the stricter reading is noted rather than coded).
